content.text:
I fixed it: in Node.js, axios now uses `timeoutErrorMessage` from the config when a request times out. The change is in the timeout handler in `lib/adapters/http.js`. If no custom message is set, it still falls back to the default `timeout of <n>ms exceeded`.

I checked it with a small script against a local server that never responds. With `timeoutErrorMessage: 'Custom'` the error message was `Custom`, and without it the message was `timeout of 200ms exceeded`. Both came back with the same error code as before (`ECONNABORTED`). I didn't run the existing test suite or add a new test.
